To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce a novel unsupervised class-incremental learning method that leverages confusion to detect incoming novel classes and 2) that we show how class-imbalance improves performance in our method.

(1) a novel class-imbalance based novelty detection method can be used to improve class-incremental learning performance, (2) a novel class-incremental loss function is effective for mitigating forgetting, and (3) our method outperforms the state-of-the-art in the unsupervised incremental learning setting on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR- 100.
(1) we propose a novel approach for continual learning that is unsupervised and (2) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across a set of commonly used image classification benchmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1. Can we learn to distinguish learned classes from new classes without any labels? 2. Can we do so in an unsupervised manner, without any additional supervision or memory?
the problem of learning in an incremental, label-agnostic setting, which we address with a novel confusion-based novelty detection method.
the following question: How can we leverage confusion to learn in an unsupervised class-incremental setting? We show that confusion can be used to learn novel classes in an unsupervised fashion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose an effective method for novelty detection in the context of class-incremental learning.
we propose a novel method to learn incrementally without any label information and show that it performs better than state of the art methods on several datasets.
our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on these benchmarks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show a novel approach to continual learning that does not require labels for the new classes.

our proposed method, called Unsupervised Class-Incemental Learning through Confusions, or UNICL, is a simple yet effective solution to the problem of continual learning with no access to class labels.
we show that a model can learn new classes incrementally without any supervision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and intuitive novelty detection method is sufficient to enable class-incremental learning in an unsupervised setting.
a simple and efficient unsupervised method can be used to improve class-incremental learning performance.
the network's own confusion is a powerful indicator that can be used to identify incoming novel classes.
